we have designed a game for measuring the effectiveness of a conversational AI agent for a specific task, and we have found evidence of a gap between AI performance in isolation and in a human-AI team setting.
while AI continues to advance in terms of performance in isolation, the human-AI team may not benefit from this progress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a human-AI team is not simply the sum of the performance of the individual AI and human components.
it is important to measure human-AIs in a human-in-the-loop setup to better understand their potential in real-world settings.
we need to design benchmarks that measure AI not just in isolation but also in terms the performance it can achieve in human-AI teams.
